utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this is a protected witness so if we may please go into private session, briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you were growing up in Vukovar during the 1980s, how did the citizens of Vukovar get along?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: How they got along? Normally, as far as I know. I was still a child at the time, attending elementary school. Everything was fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about the Borovo Selo incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: On the 2nd of May, 1991, when the policemen were killed, 12 of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what impact did this incident have on the local community in Vukovar, between the Serbs and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: What kind of an impact? Simply speaking, we wanted to join them, to stand by them, to fight for our people, for defence of homeland, for the city, for its residents, because once they were killed it was clear to us what would happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what role did you play in the defence of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I joined right away, as soon as they were killed. I joined the reserve, and we started with guard duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how old were you at this time, roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: 17 and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you join the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Reserve forces of the ZNG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were any of your other family members also in the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: My brother and I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when in your view did Vukovar come under serious attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: 27th and 28th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who attacked Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The JNA, the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how extensive was this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The planes made sorties and bombed. They also fired from tanks and all kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, if we could please go into private session briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour. And this will be Exhibit 131, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, at this time, whereabouts were people living in their homes? For example, your parents.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: In basements. The whole time, throughout the war, in basements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were defending Vukovar, how much weaponry did the defenders have compared to the JNA forces who were attacking you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Very little. Compared to what they had, we had nothing compared to their weaponry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I want to move to the time when the city was about to fall, in November. Now, roughly when did you learn that the city was about to fall and that the defenders would be withdrawing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: On the 17th, in the evening, I went to my parents', in the basement. My father told me then that the defenders had withdrawn and that they would try to break through the siege, because he himself had heard that Vukovar was about to fall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for clarification, is this the 17th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: On the 17th of November, I visited my parents, and Vukovar fell on the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you visited your parents on the 17th, what did you then do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I went back to the positions where I had been previously, and I told the defenders that Vukovar was about to fall. However, they didn't believe me. I took the telephone to call other locations, to see what we should do, but nobody responded. Nobody responded to our call. It was clear to us then that everybody had withdrawn and that Vukovar was falling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you try and break out into free territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you choose to remain in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was afraid of going to attempt to break through. Five of us remained, and it was agreed that we would go into breakthrough. However, I told them I'm not going to do that and you do as you want. I said that what ammunition I had on me I would use and leave one bullet for myself, in case Chetniks start towards the town. However, in the meantime, the situation turned around and it was the army which entered first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: That was on the 18th, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: On the 19th, in the morning, we set out while it was still dark. We set out towards the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you decide to go to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: We didn't know where our parents were, or rather, where my parents were. My friend who was with me had left his wife and children in the basement, so we agreed to go towards the hospital, to see if they were there. And this is where we were heading at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what weapons did you have on you as you headed towards the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: When I headed towards the hospital, I had no weapons. We had left the weapons behind in a basement of a house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 19th, as you made your way towards the hospital, what conditions were the buildings in, as you went there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Destroyed. Destroyed. I don't know how else to explain to you. It was a terrible sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: On our way through the centre, we saw bodies strewn on the streets of Vukovar, dead bodies. They were just lying there, not moving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you were making your way to the hospital, were you stopped by a military vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many soldiers were in the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who got out of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He asked us where we were headed. We told him we were on our way to the hospital. And then he said, "Get into our van. We'll take you there. We'll give you a ride."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at the hospital, what part of the hospital could you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was standing at the gate, or, rather, we were standing at the gate. I had a sideways glance of the hospital. I saw a part of the main gate, but for the most part I saw one of the hospital's sides, lateral wings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this include the first and second floors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what condition was the part of the hospital which you could see in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, roughly what time in the morning was this on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: It was about 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were at the gate of the hospital, roughly how many soldiers did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they regular JNA or paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did Sljivancanin order them to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question is very leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: I can rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You should, Mr. Agha, and be more careful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Sljivancanin tell the soldiers there to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Even that, Mr. Agha.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sljivancanin say anything to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He told them to keep an eye on us and that he would be sending someone to take us back to Velepromet. They kept an eye on us there. They offered us cigarettes. The whole thing took about ten minutes. And then an APC drove up and took us back to Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you stop anywhere on the way to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes. They asked us if we had any weapons and we said that we did. They asked us where the weapons were; we told them that too. And then we drove to that place. We entered the basement, got the weapons out, and surrendered them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you were taken to Velepromet. What is Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Velepromet is a warehouse, a storage facility, and once Vukovar had fallen, they assembled all the civilians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who searched you at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Velepromet, where were you taken and by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: We were taken to the death room.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, just before we move on, can I kindly ask the court clerk to again show Exhibit 59 for the witness to see. This is the same map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, if you could let us know when the map is on your screen, please. Now, on this map, you can see Velepromet marked and the JNA barracks marked. Roughly how far was Velepromet from the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: About 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in control of the JNA barracks at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I have no idea who was in control of the JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: Now, that's all with this map, so if we can take it from the screen, I would not ask for it to be exhibited since it's already 59 and the Court can refer to it for its own reference later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, coming back to Velepromet, you said, I believe, that you were taken to the room of death. Why was it called the room of death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: When we arrived at the Velepromet, they took us straight there. They searched us. They beat us a little. And then they threw us into that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how many people eventually were put into this room, roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Between 50 and 60 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And roughly how long did you stay in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any people being taken out of this room and being maltreated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Agha, I would point out that that again is a very leading question. You're working through an area I would anticipate of considerable sensitivity. Would you please take care in the way you lead the evidence from this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: I apologise to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to some of the people in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't know what happened, but whoever left the room once never came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sounds or anything did you hear when people left the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: There was a police officer there. He was sitting inside the room when we came. He had a gashing wound across his face inflicted by a knife. We asked him what had happened, and he said he'd been interrogated and his face was slashed by a knife. After sometime his name was called out again, and he went out for interrogation. We heard kicks being administered. We heard them beating him. He was begging them to stop, but they just went on with it. Finally, we heard a gurgling sound and then silence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were hearing this -- these beatings and the gurgling sound, how did this make you feel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was scared. I was only 17 at the time. I was afraid of the worst. I was afraid that someone would take a knife to me. That's what I was really afraid of. Nothing was worse than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And roughly on what date was this happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The 20th, the morning of the 20th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did there come a time when you were taken out of the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Not at this time, but later we were taken out of the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who took you out of the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The person introduced himself as a military policeman. I considered him to be a paramilitary military policeman. He took me out and another nine persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you think was going to happen to you when you were taken out of this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I thought the worst would happen to us, that they would take us to be interrogated one by one and that we would never be back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you, in fact, taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: We were taken to a different room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many others were with you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No one interrogated us at this point in time. This military policeman that walked up to me and asked me what sort of weapons I had had. I told him that I'd had a rifle. He asked me how many people I'd killed, how many Serb children I had slain, how many Serb ears I had used to make a necklace for myself, and how many fingers, severed fingers, I had used to make a necklace. I told him I'd done no such thing and that I would never have been able to do anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was watching this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: All those standing behind me, a total of 19 persons, all of them defenders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to your hands during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is also a leading question. I think this is another leading question. Just like the previous one which was also leading in nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The one particularly about the hands is merely directing attention to whether there was something particular in the way they were dealt with, and I would not regard that as leading. But the questions preceding that were, particularly the one where there was a question whether -- who interrogated you. There had been no mention of interrogation to that point, Mr. Agha. Now, you will have to pay much more attention to your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I'm trying to move quite expeditiously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened to your hands during this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: When he asked me all these things, he told me, "What do you mean you didn't do all these things? Who was it then who killed all of our soldiers?" And he started insulting me. He cursed my mother, my Ustasha mother, as he said, and he said that it would not just end like that, that we would have our come-uppance, our rightful come-uppance. He fussed around looking for handcuffs, and since he had no handcuffs on him he found a length of wire and tied my hands behind my back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone else appear during this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes. Another paramilitary came. The military policeman told him that I was a ZNG member. They called this man Topola. He gave me a bullet to bite, to swallow. He told me it was his birthday. He then left. Before he did, he looked at the 19 persons who were with me. He then came back and said, "Here is another bullet for you. Just to make sure you have a safe journey." I had to swallow that bullet too, right there in front of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who else was watching?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: All 19 of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what else did this paramilitary do to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: When he gave me those bullets to swallow, he cracked me on the head. He cursed my Ustasha mother. He said, "You deserve no better than this." He had run out of bullets so he just turned around and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move to a period when you're back in the room of death after this interrogation. Now, did there come a time when you were released from the room of death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No. They took us back to that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you had been taken back there, did there come a time when you were released from that room of death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: They didn't release us until there were too few of us remaining there. At the outset, there were 50 or 60 people there, and at this point in time there were only 38 of us left. In the meantime, a paramilitary captain appeared, at least that's how he had introduced himself. He said he would be taking us back to the barracks since the Chetniks had already killed too many people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say there was only 38 of you out of 50 or 60. What happened to the other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The other people were taken out of the room and abused outside the room. We could hear all these sounds. Then these people were taken away and never came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say this paramilitary captain came and took you out of the room. How was he able to do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't know how he was able to do this, but while we were standing outside, he addressed his men, the soldiers, telling them to keep an eye on us, not to lay a finger on any of us but to take us straight to the barracks. He said that what had happened could no longer go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you reached the JNA barracks, where were you then taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: They took us to Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of place was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: This was a civilian prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were you treated when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: While we were still on the bus, everything was normal. When we reached Mitrovica, when we reached the prison itself, they took us off the bus, and we were forced to run a gauntlet with seven or eight police officers standing on either side beating us as we were passing, kicking us, and hitting us, using their truncheons, cursing our Ustasha mother all the while. They were saying, "Fuck you and fuck Franjo Tudjman who trained you for all of this" and that we would have our come-uppance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time when you were taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: While we were lying on the ground, on the playground, our hands behind our heads and our heads down on the concrete, they were asking us questions about what we had been doing and where we had been. We answered all these questions. They were beating us, throwing us around, and then they took us to a gym where they stripped us naked. They were making sure that we had no knives or other weapons on us. And they beat us again. When we left the gym, they took us to another location closer to the prison itself. They told us to lie down on the ground, on the grass, hands behind our heads and heads down to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, whilst you were in this prison, did there come a time when you were asked to write anything down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No. We had not been asked to write anything down before we reached the prison gates. We gave no statements. It was only on the 20th of January that I was interrogated, and I was told to write down a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many statements did you write?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How truthful was this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Not truthful at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you give a truthful statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: They kept telling us that we had killed many of their people. I can't remember the specific figure that was being used. They told us to specify this in our statements, how many people we had killed, who I had been fighting for, what I had been fighting for, and what weapons I'd had. I was reluctant to tell him about that because had I told him about everything, they would have abused me even more severely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how long, roughly, did you stay in Sremska Mitrovica prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Four and a half months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on your release, what -- did there come a time when anything was said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: On our release, they told us that we would be exchanged, to get our things. When we boarded the buses, they told us that we were being taken to an exchange. The trip from Mitrovica to Nemetin was not a pleasant one. We were made to keep our hands behind our backs and head down between our knees. At Nemetin, a mere several hundred metres before the place where the exchange was to take place, a man got onto the bus and introduced himself as a captain. He said, "If we catch you again, if we capture you again, not even the Geneva Conventions will be any use to you because the next time we get you, we have the right to kill you."

utterances.speaker: MR. AGHA
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, and this completes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vasic? Cross-examined by Mr. Vasic:

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Let me introduce myself first. My name is Miroslav Vasic. I'm one of Mr. Mrksic's lawyers. Since both of us speak the language, that both of us understand, would you please make a pause after my question before you commence with your answer so that the interpreters can interpret our exchange and so that everybody else in the courtroom can follow us. This is also important in view of the protective measures granted to you so that your voice doesn't seep through my microphone. So please always make a pause after my question is completed. First of all, I'd like to turn to a technical issue. In June of 1995, did you give a statement to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This statement was typed and then shown to you, and then read out to you in the language that you understand, following which you signed it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Today, we have heard from you about where you were born and when. In view of the fact that you were a minor at the time when you found employment, I would like to know whether it was a full-time employment or were you just a contractor there? What kind of a job was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was a seasonal worker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also spoke about the composition of the residents in your neighbourhood. I would like to know whether the people you socialised with and had contacts with were people of various ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that the relations between the people who lived there were good prior to the eruption of the conflict in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your relations with your friends of other ethnicity, did they change at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Because I was in a camp at Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the time just prior to the eruption of conflict or around that time. Did the relations between you and your friends change during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Do you mean during the war itself or before the war? Because before the war, I had friends who were Serbs and Albanians, all the way up until the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when did the war begin, according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The 27th and the 28th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the war, your relations with your Serb and Albanian friends were no longer good or not as good; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Well, they are no longer in Croatia. They left Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you know when they left Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: As soon as they got Croatian papers, as soon as the agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about during the conflict? Were they in Croatia then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in the spring of 1991, members of the Serbian community started moving out of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I didn't notice that. I usually went out in a village which was near Vukovar. I didn't normally go out to locations in Vukovar. Rather, I went to this village. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a favour to ask you. If you plan to mention any locations in your answer which might reveal your identity, then please warn us so that we can go into private session. Now I would like to ask you whether you know a person called Tomislav Mercep.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Not personally, but otherwise yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on the source, do you also know what post he held in spring and summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that he had organised armed formations in Vukovar and Bogdanovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I heard about Bogdanovci. I heard about Bogdanovci, but not Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that on the 10th of March, 1991 Tomislav Mercep conducted a review of the units in the village of Bogdanovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Tomislav Mercep at one point in time was the commander of the defence of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't hear this even while you were a member of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Later on, I heard of him, but not at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now turn to May of 1991. In examination-in-chief, you described to us the event in Borovo Selo. Do you know that on the 2nd of May, 1991 several dozen of police members of Borovo Selo entered the village after the barricades had been removed and following political negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: As far as I know, 12 policemen went there and got killed. I don't know about the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you well? Are you actually saying that all of the policemen who went there got killed and that it was only 12 of them who went there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't know how many policemen went there, but based on what I understood, there were 12 of them and all 12 got killed. I wasn't there myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I know that. You said that you hadn't been there. But I would like to know whether you have ever heard that the conflict in Borovo Selo was terminated once the JNA units placed themselves between the forces of the local population in Borovo Selo and Croatian MUP, and thus prevented greater casualties. Did you ever hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that in June and July of 1991, certain persons, namely Serb residents of Vukovar, started disappearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that during that same time, there were explosions in the city of Vukovar? Did you know this even though you yourself went to Borovo Naselje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I heard detonations but I didn't know where they were coming from, from which part of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that it was the newsstands of the Borba publishing agency that were being blown up as well as the houses owned by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was the newsstand of Vjesnik that was blown up first and only then the newsstand of Borba.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about the houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear stories that in the course of July 1991, in Borovo Naselje, an operation was conducted to drive out the residents of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, you were already a member of the ZNG; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was, but not throughout the entire day. Only at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a member of the ZNG but only at night? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you elaborate on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I only stood guard at night, in the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you stood guard, you were armed; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic. There have been one or two redactions so we will need to have a half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us continue our conversation. Can you tell me if you know where the barracks in Vukovar is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in the summer of 1991, the barracks was under siege by the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that the commissioner of Croatia's government for Vukovar ordered for the water and electricity supplies and the phone lines of the barracks to be cut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I heard about the water and electricity supplies, but I have no idea who -- whose order it was pursuant to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that following that the barracks was subjected to attacks by the ZNG, who were using small arms, infantry weapons and mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about the fact that members of the JNA, in the summer of 1991, came under attack at the Vukovar post office, that they were fired on when they came to get the money for the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How did it occur to you that -- to join the ZNG following May and what had occurred in Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Since those people had been killed, I wanted to join the reserve forces of the ZNG in order to defend my country, or, rather, in order to defend my town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that at the time when you say you joined the reserve forces of the ZNG following the incident at Borovo Selo, there were no clashes in the town of Vukovar itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: There had been no clashes before the police officers were killed, or perhaps there had been some clashes and perhaps not. I can't say. I didn't go to town much. I stayed in the village. And then when the police officers were killed, I joined the ZNG. But up to that point, I had not heard of any incidents. I had not heard of any clashes between Croats and Serbs in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. From the time you joined the ZNG and onwards, May, June, July, were there any clashes in Vukovar in those months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the conflict started on the 27th of August, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes, the 27th and the 28th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is why I'm asking you if you would agree with me whether at the time you joined the ZNG, there were no clashes in Vukovar. The incident you're talking about occurred on the 2nd of May in Borovo Selo, but after that there were no further clashes for a while, can you agree with that, that all the way up until August 1991 there were no clashes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember everything. It was a long time ago, after all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do believe you. Once you'd made your decision to join the ZNG, where specifically did you go? Where did you report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I went to see Josip Tomasic [phoen] and he told me that they could not take me on because I was too young. Several days later, I again went to see him and he decided to take me on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this gentleman when you went to see him? Where was he located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: In his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was his house at Sajmiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where it was, in which neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Just across the way from my building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This gentleman that you are now talking about, did he keep any lists of ZNG members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that he decided to take you on, to allow you to join?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He told me to go home and that I would be receiving a phone call that same night and that someone would tell me where to meet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that some sort of a code word would be used or did he give you the name of the person who would call you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He said nothing. He said nothing about any code words or anything like that. He said that a place would be set and a time for our meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who called you, who telephoned you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet that person at a certain time and in a certain place, like you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met this person, the person gave you a weapon and some military equipment. Wasn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, then, what happened when you met this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He told me, "Here is my pistol. You can have it. Stay here and stand guard right here because we have no weapons to give you." No weapons had arrived or uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give you any instructions as to how you were supposed to stand guard and what it meant in practical terms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He told me to keep my eyes open and to see whether any APCs or military people were starting to arrive from the direction of the barracks towards the Slavija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about the military personnel who were in their flats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He said nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If my understanding is correct, you stood guard outside in the street, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes. In the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the building or out in the street, since you were supposed to keep a watch to see if any vehicles would be arriving? I suppose you had to be outside the building to actually see something like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The building faced the street, so -- and the road from the barracks leads just past the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was a window through which you could see the street outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you then observe? How could you see who was passing along that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was standing at the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you received this weapon, had you received any training by the ZNG? Had you been taught how to use the weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your statement that you had not done your regular military service with the JNA yet. Were you in fact able to use this pistol once you'd been given it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was never in the JNA. I was still too young for regular military service. I got this weapon from this gentleman, who then showed me how to use the weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you needed a pistol for this assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Just so I wasn't barehanded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The pistol was loaded, it had bullets in it, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ordered to shoot in certain kinds of situations while standing guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you were underage at the time you joined the ZNG. Were there any other underage persons at the time who were members of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't know. We did not have a barracks where we were all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that your brother too joined the ZNG. Did you do this together? Did he join before you or after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He joined several days before I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he an adult, technically speaking, when he joined?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much older than you is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He's two years older.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on this occasion you were given a pistol. You testified in chief that at one point you also had a rifle. Can you tell us when precisely you were given this rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was given the rifle when the war in Vukovar officially started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the rifle and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The same gentleman that I've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the same gentleman who took you on as a member of the ZNG, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he give you the rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: His place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were underage at the time. Did anyone tell you that to join a paramilitary unit like this at the time was against the constitution of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact at the time that by joining an organisation like this and by carrying a firearm, you were committing the crime of armed rebellion punishable under the then-law of the SFRY, the Criminal Code?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, up until the 27th or 28th, what kinds of assignments did you have as a member of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I worked during daytime and I stood guard at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that, among the ZNG members, groups had been organised to execute people at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when did you join a ZNG unit for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I joined the reserve forces of the National Guards Corps, the ZNG, on the 3rd of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That was the ZNG. What I want to know is when did you come for the first time to a ZNG unit. When did you start serving in a unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: On the 27th of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did somebody then invite you to join? And would you also please tell us where did you join a ZNG unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Nobody invited me to join. There was the shelling of the town, the town was bombed by planes, and I went into a basement, and after a certain period of time, the same person told me that I should get my things and go to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to this, did you hear that on the 24th of August two planes of the air force had been shot down above Borovo Naselje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I heard that the planes were downed, but I don't know on what day and where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will now ask you about the line, the front line, where you went to serve. If you believe that this can lead to your identity being revealed, then please warn me so that we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Ask away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you went with the gentleman whom you have mentioned to the front line, to the combat line. Would you please tell us where this line was located on the 27th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: It was the Stjepan Supanc elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 59, which is map number 6? My learned friend from the Prosecution has already shown this map to the witness earlier today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the map now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to give the witness a pen so that he can mark the line on the map as it was on the 27th of August, 1991. Could we zoom in in the downtown area, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark with a cross the spot or the area where the line was, where your unit was deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You put a circle and a letter A?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us, do you know where other units were located, other units of the ZNG, in this area, the area where you yourself were and also in the neighbourhood called Sajmiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No. I had no information regarding that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you change the deployment position of your unit throughout that period of time while combat operations in Vukovar lasted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will not be needing this map any longer but, Your Honours, I would like to have it exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 27th of August, 1991 you took up positions at the school. Can you tell us how many members of your unit were deployed there at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, the last map marked will be Exhibit 132.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these positions secured in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You dug out trenches, you put sand sacks there, you also had shelters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in addition to that, you had an observation post, didn't you, at your positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we better go into private session, Your Honour, because I'm about to ask who else was a member of the unit, in addition to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that at one point in time you heard Tomislav Mercep was the commander of the town's defence. Can you tell us when you heard this? When was the first time you heard this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Must have been September or October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Tomislav Mercep was called back to Zagreb, did you hear that the commissioner, Marin Vidic, was in charge of the town's defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that at one point in time Mile Dedakovic, aka Jastreb, was the commander of the town's defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I heard something about that but I don't remember the month or anything. It wasn't for me to know who was there and who wasn't. All I had to worry about was the front line and the commander was there for everything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you did not know where the orders were coming from to your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that during combat operations, in addition to the ZNG and the MUP units, HOS units were also involved in these operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout these combat operations, at the line that you were holding, you never met a single member of the HOS? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes. Not one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Stjepan Rados? Are you familiar with the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I'm not familiar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your time at the front line, did you at any point hear that the Vukovar defence Main Staff had all left Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the road from the barracks to the hospital? Did that road pass the location at which you were holding the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 13th of October, 1991 did you perhaps receive an order to remove the barricades, to clear the road of the barricades so -- not to clear the barricades although a humanitarian convoy was supposed to pass there, so that you would not disturb the lines of defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No. No one told us anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that this humanitarian convoy did not pass the -- along the road near your checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't remember. After we stood guard, we would rest in the cellar. This may have happened while I was in the cellar but I don't know. I heard nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned a cellar. Is that in the elementary school or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: In the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know which unit was stationed at the palace of Count Eltz?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There is one thing I'd like to clarify now. This is in relation to the 17th of November, 1991. I'll try to do this in such a way that we can do it in public session. You told my colleague that on the 17th of November you went to that place you mentioned. You told him that you went there in the evening hours. Do you remember telling the investigator of the OTP in your statement in 1991 that on -- 1995, that on the 17th, you went to that same place in the morning hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I said that in my testimony here also, that I went there on the 17th in the morning and not in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you tell us today that it was in the evening hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about your unit at the time? Did it still have any links to Vukovar's main defence staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: We had the field phone that we were using, but we no longer had any Motorola. There was no electricity to recharge the batteries, and all we had left was the field phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us about what you heard on the 17th of November 1991, when you went to that place. What I'd like to ask you now is: You told us about this person who conveyed this piece of information to you. Can you tell us if that person too was a member of any military unit during combat operations in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No. That person was not a member of any unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout this time, was this person in the cellar where you found him on the -- on 17th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that this person told you on that day that everybody from Vukovar's main defence staff had left in a bid to escape to Vinkovci and break through the siege?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you where he got the information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us this in public session or should we go into private?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then please tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: A policeman came to visit them, and he told them all weapons and any Croatian items that they had, meaning anything with chequer-board symbol and flags, should be removed because Vukovar was about to fall. He said that if they found anything on anyone, he couldn't vouch for what would happen to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You did not receive this information via telephone from your superior command, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No. My commander was absent. I don't know where he was. Therefore, we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us since when was your commander absent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Since the morning hours. He only came in the evening, saying that nobody was manning the lines and that the -- that Vukovar was about to fall and that we had to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you then that you could withdraw to the hospital or that another option would be to attempt to break through the siege and go to Vinkovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He told us whoever wants to go into breakthrough can go. Those who do not want that should go into basements. Some went into breakthrough; some didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, he didn't mention a possibility of having members of the ZNG go to the hospital where they were awaiting an evacuation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, why did you go to the hospital on the 19th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I went to the hospital because, on the 18th, in the morning, my parents were no longer in the basement. I didn't know where they were, so I headed towards the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why hospital? Why that place specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Because my neighbour worked at the hospital, a lady neighbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, you assumed that they had gone to the hospital together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I didn't assume anything. It's just that my neighbour and I headed towards the hospital, because we didn't know where they were. We thought that they might have gone there. But they were not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before the hospital, did you first go to the municipal building where the main defence staff of Vukovar was, to acquire some information about what to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before going to the hospital, did you first go to the MUP building where a ZNG unit had been stationed as well as a MUP unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that before going to the hospital, you went -- you left the school where you'd been manning the line, and you went to your apartment. Why did you go there first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I went home to change clothes. My jeans were dirty, and I put on another T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you wear yellow shoes manufactured in Borovo on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was on the 19th in the morning. Isn't it true that the JNA units had entered that part of the town already on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Weren't you afraid of moving about armed in the part of the town that at that time was under the control of the JNA forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: At the time, there was no one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to your apartment with a weapon, wanting to have a change of clothes and prepare to shoot if you came across anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left your apartment, armed, you went to the hospital, taking the main road; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes. But first we hid our weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, where did you hide your weapons and how far is it from the place where you changed your clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Several hundred metres from my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not alone, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who was with you, did that person also have a change of clothes and did that person also leave their weapon in the same location as you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He didn't change his clothes. He just hid his weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who was with you, is he a Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did that person go to the hospital? You gave us your reasons. Why did this other person go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He was looking for his wife and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While en route from the place where you hid your weapons to the hospital, how many people did you come across before crossing the Vuka River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: We hid our weapons in a place where we didn't see anything else. While we were crossing the Vuka River, there was nothing either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you didn't meet anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you change your clothes and discard your weapon before going to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Because it was torn and dirty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it because wearing clean clothes you wouldn't appear as somebody who took part in combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you discard your weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: We didn't want to have it on us while going to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that starting on the 17th of November and until the 20th of November, members of the ZNG and MUP who remained in Vukovar, came to hospital en masse, discarded their weapons there, changed their uniforms, took off their clothes and put white coats on, trying to pass themselves as help workers at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I wasn't informed about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't informed about that during the relevant period of time. However, after the events, did you hear this from anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Once I left the camp, I heard about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know if this is an appropriate time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We had thought to go another five minutes, but is that inconvenient? It is? Very well. For you, Mr. Vasic, we'll break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will continue where we left it before the break. You said that following your departure from Mitrovica, or your release from Mitrovica, you learned about the fact that the members of the ZNG and MUP had changed clothes in the hospital and put on white clothing in order to look like help workers. Please tell me, who told you this? Was it one of your fellow soldiers or any medical staff people who told you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: When we left Mitrovica, he came to Zagreb, and in the corridor I heard a conversation. They were saying that they had changed clothes. I don't know the names of these people, because I met a lot of people at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At one point you said that you had one wounded person at your defence line or combat line. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this wounded person, did he ever reach the hospital, and if so, how was he transported there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: He didn't go to the hospital. It was a slight wound. He remained at the positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who treated him there at the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: The commander just bandaged his arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this one of the three persons who went to break through the siege, as you've described to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the three persons who went to break through the siege, if I understood you well, only two others remained, which was you and your friend; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of you was wounded. Can you tell us who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: That person had withdrawn earlier. None of the two of us was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the 19th of November, did you ever visit the hospital? I mean after the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1995, when you gave your statement to the OTP investigators, did you tell them that prior to the 19th of November, you had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was wounded but not badly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you the person who had a slight wound and who was treated by the commander and who remained there at the positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If my math is correct, then your unit had more than one wounded member; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: When I was wounded, I could still move, but he was hit in the arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said he was hit in the arm. I assume that he too would have been able to move, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us try to sum up. Your unit had more than one wounded, did it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I didn't consider myself to be wounded. It was just a slight injury or a cut, if you like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't count that as a wounding, in your testimony today, but why did you refer to that as a wound when you talked to the investigators of the OTP in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Because I had been hit by shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you spoke to your fellow fighters, you said there was an option to attempt a breakthrough, an escape, or there was an option to stay behind. Why did you not go and attempt to break through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I was very young and I was scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you not scared to walk around on the 18th and 19th, walk around the streets of Vukovar, given the fact that the JNA had entered the town on the 18th and that they were armed? Or that you were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact whether I had a weapon me or not, I still was scared. I had no idea what would become of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just another fact that needs clarifying with regard to this and then we'll move on to a different subject. You said that on the 18th the JNA entered the area and got as far as the Vuka River. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I wrote in my statement that the JNA entered the town, but I never said how far they got.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us now, if you know, which point they reached on the 18th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you informed your fellow fighters on the 17th, on the evening of the 17th, did you know which lines of defence had been pierced and how far the JNA had advanced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: When I told my fellow fighters that Vukovar was about to fall, at that time I had no idea if they -- there was still any roads open for us to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But did you know how far the JNA had advanced at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: They still hadn't reached town on the 17th, not any of the neighbourhoods that were part of the town proper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 18th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: They were advancing from every direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's between your neighbourhood -- your positions and the Vuka River, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I'm not sure if they got as far as the river, but that certainly was the case where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said today that the next day, on the 19th of November, you passed through that area where you now say that the JNA forces had already arrived. You said you were moving down the main street and that you did not come across a single soldier up until the point where you reached the Vuka River; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: It was on the 18th that they entered the town. I don't know how far they got. But on the 19th, my fellow fighter and I headed for the hospital on the morning of the 18th and we met no one along the way.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: On the morning of the 19th, the interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Just a minute, please. My apologies. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move on to the part of your testimony that concerns Velepromet. First of all, can you please describe where the room was that you were brought to on the 19th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do so, if you can. If you can describe from the entrance on, as it were, where exactly was that room and what sort of a building was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: You took the entrance and went straight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is what I'm interested in. If you take the main gate of Velepromet, which side of the main gate was the building in which you were kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Once I'd entered, I just kept on walking straight and I never took any turns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you talking about the entrance to the building or the main gate of Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Once you pass the main gate, you walk straight across the courtyard, in order to reach that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that room in a brick building or in a hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: In a brick building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said today that the room was referred to as the "death room." Why did you not say that to the investigator in 1995 when you spoke to him about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I said it was called the death room because whoever entered was captured and those who left the room never came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you share this with the investigators back in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it refresh your memory if I gave you a copy of your statement to go through and check? Perhaps you can try and find any references that you may have made to this death room, as you now appear to be calling it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: This building was a warehouse, a storage facility. We nicknamed it the death room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. But what I'm talking about is did you share this with the OTP investigator or did you not? That's all I'm asking. Do you remember the fact that you forgot to share that with the investigator back when you talked to him in 1995? That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please? I would like to show the witness his own statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at page 3 and part of page 4? You talk about Velepromet. The last portion of page 3 and the beginning of page 4. Have you had a look?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any reference that you made to this room that you were kept in as "the death room"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell the OTP investigator that out of the 60 people who were there, only 38 made it and the rest disappeared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does your statement not indicate that the rest of them went missing after they had been taken outside, or does your statement only indicate that the 38 persons including you were transferred to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Whoever came out never came back. There were 38 of us remaining there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does your statement not say that whoever went out never came back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: I can't remember all the things that I wrote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a need to go back to your statement? Maybe you would like to have a copy to check.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: If it's no problem, I'd like to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-032
utterances.text: Please repeat your question.
